result: I found disorder in the isopropanol solvent molecule (O3/C31–C33) and modelled it as two positions. In the ordered model its three carbons had extreme displacement parameters: Ueq was 0.21–0.46 Å² and the ADP anisotropy ratios reached about 9–11. Several residual peaks also sat beside them. I kept O3 in one position and split C31/C32/C33 into PART 1 and PART 2. The two parts' occupancies are tied to a free variable, each part has its own riding hydrogens, and the carbons are refined isotropically. DFIX/DANG restraints hold the bond lengths and angles, and SIMU keeps the displacement parameters similar. A first attempt with RIGU failed with a singular matrix, so I dropped it. The occupancies refined to 0.66/0.34, the carbons' Ueq fell to 0.11–0.19 Å², and the fit improved with only two extra parameters: R1 went from 0.0741 to 0.0707, wR2 from 0.210 to 0.200, and GooF from 1.17 to 1.12. One minor issue remains: the engine left C31B's hydrogen at its starting position because of a bond-count mismatch. The 4-methylcyclohexyl ring also has elongated displacement parameters, but its nearby residual peaks are small (≤0.42 e/Å³) and sit between atoms rather than at alternative positions. I judged it ordered and left the rest of the model unchanged.
